subject.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `durable.mode` and the shared durable-runtime persistence/recovery contract as a supported core product surface?
rationale: The branch is not a narrow repair: it adds persistent cross-owner execution evidence, recovery authority, fail-closed behavior, and configuration that establish a long-lived product and operational contract.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded durable core
options.body: Approve the owner-first, opt-in durable contract and require an explicit upgrade, retention, and operator-support plan across the stacked PRs.

options.title: Defer the product surface
options.body: Keep the proposal unmerged until maintainers choose a narrower supported problem and ownership boundary.

options.title: Reject core adoption
options.body: Decline the shared durable runtime in core and pursue only independently justified, owner-local reliability fixes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded durable core
recommendation.body: Approve the owner-first, opt-in durable contract and require an explicit upgrade, retention, and operator-support plan across the stacked PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: No established current-main owner for this proposed core subsystem is evidenced in the supplied history; repository leadership must choose the product boundary.
